I wanted to clear the air about Alabama's QB battle.

A pundit came out recently and proclaimed Alec Morris the frontrunner in the 'Bama QB race, and immediately several outlets jumped on the story. CollegeSpun screengrabbed Zenitz's twitter on friday, and CBS wrote the following yesterday:

According to AL.com, it is Morris, not Coker, who leading the competition after the Tide's second scrimmage of the fall on Saturday.

Ignoring the typo in that passage, the average reader might be shocked to learn that Jake Coker, the strong-armed QB from FSU who almost started last year, is floundering in the QB competition, and that Morris (unheard of by nonfans until now) is on track to start against Wisconsin.

LOL

Did these guys even watch the A-Day game in the spring? I saw some raw talent, and a lot of mistakes by inexperienced guys, but I also saw Coker and Cornwell combine for more than half the completions in the game, and the only two passing TDs. I saw some errant throws by Morris, and some costly mistakes by Bateman (a 5-star recruit) that had probably driven Saban to practice him with the WRs earlier that month.

See, here's the crazy thing, and the reason this story has legs: Saban hates mistakes. Especially turnovers, and Morris had none in the A-Day game, while Coker and Cornwell combined for three. Recently, Saban has been praising Morris' play, but only in as much as Saban is capable of praising any of his players in the preseason. Reading into Saban's comments on one of his players is like reading into a politician's comments on one of his policies.

For example:

"Alec has done a nice job all [preseason]...I think he does a really good job of understanding the offense. He helps the other players play better. And I think that he has probably shown command at the position, which I think is important. We've just got to continue to work on touch, accuracy, efficiency. But I've been really pleased with what Alec has done in this camp."

Sounds great, right? Or does it? Eh. In the same motion that Saban praised Morris' leadership ("command at the position"), he criticized his talent ("work on touch, accuracy, efficiency").

And it's the Saban element that makes this situation a gigantic mindfuck. He just told the media to piss off, so what can you really believe from the media right now, which is the only view we have through the Nick Saban Firewall. We have to try and balance two untrustworthy sources, both of which are telling us Morris may or may not be talented enough to unseat Coker (who is much more talented), and both of which now tell us that Cornwell is out of the picture...

Wait, what?

Yeah, apparently David Cornwell, another former 5-star QB (and #3 in nation in 2013), is no longer a contestant, which is weird since he was the frontrunner two weeks ago.

See what I'm talking about?

We didn't know AJ McCarron was the starter in 2011 until 2-3 games in, and we didn't now Blake Sims was a starter last year until he destroyed Florida. I've been saying this since the end of last season: We won't know the Alabama starting QB until the first conference game (Ole Miss, Week 3).

All this talk about Morris is because they haven't talked about him yet. It's Saban's last bluff before the season starts. If Blake Barnett weren't a freshman (and a legit contender as he builds weight), he'd be a bluff too. Hell, Saban even hinted that he'd start a Frosh if he proved himself, so there's another layer to this maze.

Saban will pick the QB that leads the team, puts them in a position to score, and doesn't turn the ball over. From what I've seen in practice film and spring game footage, Morris doesn't make many mistakes because he doesn't take any risks. He does this because Saban no doubt has pointed to Blake Sims' stupid throws last year against Ole Miss, Auburn, and OSU as reasons for close games/losses. But Morris doesn't have Sims feet or Coker's arm. He doesn't have McCarron's leadership, or McElroy's accuracy. He's just plain ole Alec Morris, and while I love him b/c he's our QB (RTR dude), I think "balanced" is a euphemism for "bland."

Saban liked bland when he got to Alabama (he didn't turn AJ loose until the NCG in 2011), but Kiffin doesn't. His offenses are pass-happy, that's one of the reasons we lost to OSU. Kiffin needs a QB who can distribute the ball in space and over heads. If Morris wins the job, it's because they expect his talent to finally catch up with his "efficiency," another Saban euphemism for not turning the ball over.

Tell me what you think. Your guess is as good as mine.
